scope: Local 250-entry usage preview. Current learner-relevant senses and constructions; not every dictionary sense or a claim of perfect synonymy.
method: Read the earlier contrast evidence, expand the comparisons with authored English explanations and Spanish/English examples, and directly check targeted DLE/DPD entries and original research. Each published preview section carries its own relevant source links. Retrieval below records access, not independent linguistic review or proof that every sense of an entry was examined.
reviewDecisions: Saber/conocer share some factual knowledge contexts; use constructions and acquaintance context rather than a universal facts/familiarity exclusion.
Entender/comprender overlap in intellectual and interpersonal understanding. Do not impose a superficial/deep rule.
Empezar/comenzar share a + infinitive and por + infinitive constructions. Corpus register and regional preferences are tendencies, not answer exclusions.
Preserve the eight-word prompt policies and reuse the earlier 250-entry recall policy for other cards; comparison membership never derives accepted answers.
Use current DPD qualifications for deber (de), regional gente, leísmo, and regional hasta; avoid universal claims based on introductory rules.
Agua remains feminine with el; mano is feminine despite -o. Noun gender testing is not implemented by this preview.
DPD comenzar only establishes conjugation, so construction evidence also uses DPD empezar and the University of Santiago de Compostela database manual.
The guessed DPD según entry does not exist; source its semantics from DLE and pronoun selection from DPD pronombres personales tónicos.
Main-card examples for the original eight are retained; remaining grouped cards use frozen existing sentence examples; the 38 standalone cards use the new authored examples.
implementation: lemmas/data/day1-usage.json plus the existing detailed temporal comparison; 250 unique deck IDs, 60 comparison groups, 38 standalone usage notes, and the separate después/luego deep comparison.
validationLimits: Automated tests verify coverage, data structure, scope and grading boundaries. They do not prove linguistic accuracy. Spanish examples and English explanations are authored, not quotations or independent expert certification.
